brief: Morgan Stanley's economists expect the Fed, after hiking 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16, to hike again in December and March, then hold at 4.25-4.50% through end-2027, one hike below market pricing's 4.73% end-2027 upper bound versus MS's own 4.41% probability-weighted path. Because the 10-year yield has tracked Fed-path pricing closely since mid-2023, that gap implies 10-year yields about 30bp below forwards by end-2027 (4.70% versus 5.11% on September 23), with the 2-year at 4.50%. As the Fed holds at its peak and core PCE cools, 2-year yields should fall more than 10-year yields, steepening 2s10s to about 20bp. Risks skew toward lower yields: the bull case, a recession scenario with oil at $140-160/barrel and 200bp of cuts, puts the 10-year at 3.80%, while the bear case, a demand shock with the Fed at 5.00-5.25%, puts it at 5.30% at peak. A moderate oil-price rise would lift yields via more hikes, but a large spike would push the Fed toward cuts instead. Treasuries are also forecast to modestly underperform swaps through 2027.
